verdicts.explanation: The paper states that Na3.4Hf0.8Zr0.8In0.3Ga0.1(SiO4)2(PO4) and Na3.5Hf1.5In0.4Ga0.1(SiO4)2(PO4) had room-temperature total conductivities of 0.7 and 0.3 mS/cm, with activation energies of 0.34 and 0.33 eV, in that order. The record's null measurement_temperature_C is not an error under the schema, since the paper gives only 'room temperature' and no numeric value appears in the quote.

The 0.3 mS/cm total conductivity and 0.33 eV activation energy are assigned to the second composition, Na3.5Hf1.5In0.4Ga0.1(SiO4)2(PO4), which matches the order in the sentence. The data origin is experimental and the room-temperature context is correct.

The paper states that the bulk ionic conductivities of the two compositions were 3.96 and 3.17 mS/cm, in that order, and the surrounding text places these at room temperature. The Na3.4Hf0.8Zr0.8In0.3Ga0.1 assignment by order is correct.
The second bulk value, 3.17 mS/cm, belongs to Na3.5Hf1.5In0.4Ga0.1(SiO4)2(PO4) by order. The record is experimental and the room-temperature context is consistent with the paper.

The paper states that Na3.5Hf0.7In1.2Ge0.1(SiO4)1.3(PO4)1.7 yielded only 0.01 mS/cm total ionic conductivity. The record is experimental, and the null temperature and secondary fields are not contradicted.

field_errors.evidence: The bulk ionic conductivities of these compositions are comparable to state-of-the-art Na NASICON56 (~5 mS/cm for optimized Na3.4Zr2(SiO4)2.4(PO4)0.6)

verdicts.explanation: The ~5 mS/cm value belongs to the literature-cited optimized Na3.4Zr2(SiO4)2.4(PO4)0.6, not to the measured Na3.5Hf0.7In1.2Ge0.1(SiO4)1.3(PO4)1.7 sample named in material_as_written. The material is therefore wrong, even though the literature_cited origin is correct.
